newsitem.title: USA: OfficeMax says cost controls helped Q3.
newsitem.headline: OfficeMax says cost controls helped Q3.

text.p: OfficeMax Inc said Tuesday tight cost controls more than offset a third-quarter gross margin decline. Computer sales increased 25-30 percent on a same-store basis, it said.

"Our third quarter operating results reflect continued very tight cost controls and the ongoing leveraging of store operating and selling expenses," chairman Michael Feuer said in a statement. Expenses as a percentage of sales declined 66 basis points from the previous year to 15.3 percent, he said.
He said gross margins declined due to increased sales as a percent of total merchandise mix of lower-margin computers.

As reported earlier, OfficeMax said it earned $0.19 a share in the quarter versus the year-ago $0.15 excluding last year's sale of the company's interest in Corporate Express. Sales rose 27 percent to $849.8 million, it said.
The stock was up 3/8 to 13-7/8 with more than 1.1 million shares traded by midmorning.
OfficeMax has 530 office supply stores, some including FurnitureMax furniture departments and CopyMax copy centers.

Feuer, who is also chief executive officer, said the company is pleased with the results, particularly in light of a decline in retail paper prices from a year ago. Also, he said, last year's third quarter benefitted from the introduction of the Microsoft Windows 95 software launch.
He said the quarter reflects higher sales from new store openings, continued sales gains in the maturing store base and the spreading of fixed costs over higher sales volumes.

It is pleased with its current inventory position and merchandise assortment heading into the holiday selling season, he said. In the past quarter, overall inventories grew in line with plan to approximately match overall sales growth.
He said computer inventories grew about 10 percent less than computer sales, significantly improved over last year.
